summary: Implemented GeneralizedWassersteinDiceLoss per the spec. Changes: (1) monai/losses/dice.py: added numpy and torch.nn.functional imports; new class after GeneralizedDiceLoss with constructor (dist_matrix, reduction), helpers wasserstein_distance_map, compute_weights_generalized_true_positives, compute_generalized_true_positive, compute_denominator, and forward returning the batch mean; alias generalized_wasserstein_dice added after generalized_dice. (2) monai/losses/__init__.py: exports GeneralizedWassersteinDiceLoss (import wrapped in parentheses to stay under 120 columns). (3) tests/test_generalized_wasserstein_dice_loss.py: binary 2D test (correct, size-1 channel target, flipped) and empty-class test (correct, flipped), 1e-3 tolerance. Nothing was run or committed, per instructions. Verified by reading only: hand-computed the batch-of-two case as TP=0.8, D=2.4, loss about 0.333, matching the spec. A line-length grep found only one pre-existing over-120 line in dice.py (line 36), not mine. Choices: the forward squeezes the target's channel axis only when target rank equals input rank; the distance matrix is cast to the probability dtype as well as device; TP and D use the explicit (batch, batch, N) product.
